dedupe_keys.name: monza and brianza green infrastructure suitability map for sustainable urban drainage sustainability 2021

description: This study builds a Green Infrastructure Suitability Map for the province of Monza and Brianza in Lombardy, Italy, to show where nature-based drainage can relieve the sewer network. Researchers from the University of Milan and the University of Milano-Bicocca worked with the consultancy Studio Geologia Sacchi and the water utility BrianzAcque, and published it in Sustainability on 27 May 2021. Coverage is the province at municipal detail. A three-phase method first produces base maps of green areas, natural infiltration potential and exclusion areas, then combines them into the suitability map. Format and access: an open access article with the maps as figures. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: the map layers are not published as data files, and the method relies on regional geological inputs. It is an example of utility-led adaptation planning for green and blue infrastructure. Related catalogue records are the BGS Infiltration SuDS Map, a national equivalent in Britain, and the CIRIA SuDS Manual.
